_comment: ComponentCatalog UI-TEST scene DEFINITION (201F4F51 template-free). A left nav rail of bookmarks beside a RIGHT scroll TRAY: every component in its own card box, all present, flowing in a scrollable `list`; a bookmark scrolls the tray to that card (card_i.y - card_0.y), the top card's bookmark highlights. The standalone `tabs` control is RETIRED here — superseded by the PTT (paged_menu); the Paged Menu card demos the real nested page->tab behavior (Page 1: Tab 1/Tab 2, Page 2: Tab 3/Tab 4) via two page-gated `pill_toggle` tab rails (the PTT lays out the first VISIBLE rail). The Nav Footer card's BACK/NEXT buttons fire the SAME cat_pm_page_prev/next names the page rail steps on and the root's on_page_prev/next intents fire — one signal name, every trigger. FOUR SECTIONS: the roster-derived KIND cards (0-27), then the RECIPES page (28-39: the canonical arrangements the catalog documents without promoting a kind), the FILLERS page (40-45: each engine-crate surface filler seated live on a plain `surface`) and the MODALS page (46-47: one button per shared tree in scenes/shared/, opened through the SharedModal host seam, with the modal_closed answer read back). 48 cards, every one with its bookmark. Display strings are $tokens; interactive VALUES ride binds the bench seeds + folds; the paged-menu visibility binds are derived in the PAIR SCRIPT (componentcatalog.lua) from the page/tab. The bench owns + loads this file.

cat_gadget_stage._comment: One of the two 3D stages the FILLERS page seats (the other is `cat_doll_stage`); both are ordinary stage sources the catalog reads through `stages.<source>`, exactly as every other bench does. The Gadget card's surface — one lit `scene` pass into the surface colour, cleared to the void so the card's panel reads behind it. Nothing is drawn but the gadget's own overlay lines, which is the point: the handles ARE the demo.

cat_doll_stage._comment: The Doll card's surface — the Loomforge portrait shot, ring and all. The catalog uploads no rig, so the ring is what draws; a consumer that sets a rig gets the character in the same seat with no stage change.

children._comment: THE DISMISSABLE TOGGLE (ruling DA0E1B57), demonstrated: `dismissable_bind` names a Model key, the checkbox below writes it, and the walker reads it at its Cancel routing — so turning the box OFF makes THIS slab refuse Esc / pad-B, exactly as busy.lua does to the shared busy modal while its work runs. The prop defaults TRUE: a slab that authors neither is always dismissable.
children.title: $cat_popup_title
children.subtitle: $cat_popup_sub

children._comment: BINDING ICON (Aaron 2026-09-02): the tooltip affordance as its own kind — give it an ActionSignal and it shows the CURRENT DEVICE's face of the binding (atlas glyph on a pad, the house keycap on kbm) with a `{Signal}` help label. Read-only chrome: never focusable, never a target. The three rows read LIVE bindings the scene publishes; a signal no profile binds shows its own name.

RECIPES PAGE (B05B3D09 §4b, Aaron's Q3 = YES): the canonical ARRANGEMENTS the catalog documents as the registry of record. Every card below names only roster kinds and resolves only shared style blocks — a recipe is the answer to "that looks like a duplicate kind" (F1BFA408): decompose before promoting.
RECIPE — toast + Undo: panel > row > text + button. The transient message and its ONE verb.
RECIPE — property row: text + one editor. Metadata editing (402A4B93 #16) is a stack of these, never a `kv_row` kind (retired, DCA4DFB2).

RECIPE — tree row: a caret button + a name button, and the DEPTH is an ARRANGE BIND (`<id>_off_x`, published by componentcatalog.lua) on an anchored cell — a hierarchy is rows + an indent value, never a nest of containers and never a `tree_row` kind.
RECIPE — breadcrumb: a `row` with `rows_from` over ONE button prototype. The path is DATA (the bench publishes the crumbs), so a deeper path is more rows and never more tree.
RECIPE — notice card: a severity panel over a glyph text + the copy. The SEVERITY is the glyph's colour token, not a kind (`notice_card` retired, DCA4DFB2).
RECIPE — transport bar: three verbs and a readout. The time controls of every timeline consumer (Loomforge TAE, the DM wave editor, the GM clock).
RECIPE — resource readout bar: a `resource_gauge` and its number. The Dungeon Maker's top strip is a row of these (B05B3D09 §3B).
RECIPE — command card: a `grid` of `action_slot`. The RTS command card and the adventurer's hotbar are the same arrangement at two densities.
RECIPE — legend row: a `stat_dot` and its label, once per series. Layer legends, status keys and the sim-viz map key are all this.
RECIPE — collapsible group: a header button that flips a Model flag, and a `cell` behind the matching `visible_bind`. The DS group header, with no `collapsible` prop promoted.

RECIPE — DRAG → DROP (the walker's drag channel, F652B72F): a `drag_kind` source and a `drop_accept` + `drop_action` target. Both channels are live here — a pointer release over the target, and a pad Confirm on the focused target while a payload is carried.

FILLERS PAGE (B05B3D09 §4d, Aaron's Q1 = fillers, not kinds): each engine-crate surface filler seated LIVE on a plain `surface` — the RigView / WorldMap pattern. The catalog is the registry of record for these too (A466E4C7).
FILLER — Plot (110D345F, flicker_widgets::Plot): the same demo series read three ways. Seated on a plain `surface` by rect; the ink comes off this scene's `plot` style block.
FILLER — GraphCanvas (E5721AE6, flicker_canvas::GraphCanvas): three demo nodes with one SELF-LOOP. Drag a card, wheel to zoom about the cursor, middle-drag to pan.
FILLER — Timeline (E5721AE6, flicker_canvas::Timeline): seven lanes carrying span and point events under a moving playhead. Wheel zooms about the frame under the cursor.

FILLER — Gadget (7811D68B, flicker_rigview::Gadget over a RigView surface): the ONE 3D manipulation overlay, in translate mode over an empty rig. Aim → Locked → Modify colours each handle from this scene's `gadget` style block.

FILLER — Doll (D708485E, flicker_rigview::Doll): the small-panel skinned-rig preview on its authored stage. The catalog uploads no rig (a rig is bench content), so the card shows the doll's authored ground ring, live on the per-surface clock.

MODALS PAGE (1F0F7347 + DE51BC4B): one button per shared tree under scenes/shared/, each opened by id through `SharedModal::open` with demo params. The catalog is the EXERCISER of the seam — `settings` is the one exemption (it is the settings SCREEN, not a modal).
The SharedModal seam's answer channel, read back: `Scene::modal_closed(modal, result, payload)` folded into two bound readouts. Open any modal above and its verdict lands here.

notice._comment: A notice's SEVERITY as a colour token — the recipe card's glyph points here instead of a `notice_card` kind carrying its own palette (DCA4DFB2 retired that kind; 790872EE keeps colour in the one palette).

plot._comment: The Plot filler's ink (110D345F): the filler owns no palette — it takes finished rgba, and these point at ui_theme.json tokens like every other block.

canvas._comment: The GraphCanvas filler's colour slots (E5721AE6). CanvasStyle is nothing but slots the consumer fills; blank() is transparent, which is 'unset' rather than a colour choice.
canvas.label: $ink_bright

timeline._comment: The Timeline filler's strip colours (E5721AE6). Each lane's own four colours come off `stat_dot.hues.<hue>` so a lane's ink and a legend dot's ink are literally the same token.

gadget._comment: The Gadget overlay's STATE colours (7811D68B): the three axes at rest, then the Aim -> Locked -> Modify machine and the refused handle. GadgetStyle holds no colour of its own.
